paper.title_en: Loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ at NLO+PS for LHC simulations: exact, fast scale and PDF event weights, theory uncertainties, and the limits of rescaled LO+PS
paper.abstract_en: We study loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ production with charged-lepton and neutrino $Z$ decays at next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD matched to parton showers, using public software at $\sqrt{s}=13$ and 13.6 TeV. An exact loop-amplitude cache reduces event-generation time by a factor of 26 with 450 scale and PDF weights, while Born suppression improves boosted-event statistics without changing the weighted prediction. We present inclusive results for both channels and charged-lepton differential and STXS Stage 1.3 predictions with theory uncertainties. At 13.6 TeV, fixed-order top-quark mass-scheme variations transferred to NLO+PS dominate the statistically precise central-Higgs STXS bins for $p_\mathrm{T}^V\ge150$ GeV, reaching 32-50%. An inclusive $K$ factor does not reproduce the boosted and jet-dependent NLO+PS spectra of the tested LO+PS samples, and the differences depend strongly on the shower prescription. For specified CMS- and ATLAS-style vetoed sources at 13.6 TeV, we construct separate charged-lepton and neutrino corrections using ensembles of gradient-boosted classifiers, with calibration, target-theory variations and transfer uncertainties. Independent tests show substantial improvement over inclusive rescaling in most tested distributions, but not uniform closure. In charged-lepton calibration comparisons, the median STXS uncertainty from transported NLO scales and transfer terms is 17% for both the CMS- and ATLAS-style corrections, compared with LO scale uncertainties of 28% and 26% at fixed $K$. These comparisons do not include the complete target-theory budget. The corrections do not restore the depleted hard-recoil population; the highest ATLAS-style $p_\mathrm{T}^H$ bin stays below NLO+PS even at the upper edge of its band. The setup, reference results, and source- and channel-specific models support new NLO+PS generation and reuse of existing samples within stated limits.
